General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১) Optical fibers are mainly used for which of the following?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Optical fibers are mainly used in telecommunications, but they are also used for lighting, sensors, toys, and special cameras for seeing inside small spaces. They are sometimes used in medicine to see inside people, like down their throat.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২) Wood is the main raw material for the manufacture of
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Paper is a thin sheet material produced by mechanically and/or chemically processing cellulose fibres derived from wood, rags, grasses or other vegetable sources

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩) Nuclear fission is caused by the impact of:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: In nuclear fission neutron is bumbarded on heavy metal like plutonium, urenium. In this process large amount of heat energy is produced.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪) The dark lines in the solar spectrum are due to-
General Science & Technology (Full).option1: ক) Absorption of corresponding wavelengths by the prism used in the photograph.
General Science & Technology (Full).option2: খ) Absence of corresponding wavelengths from the light emitted by the core of the sun
General Science & Technology (Full).option3: গ) Absorption of corresponding wavelengths by the outer layers of the sun.
General Science & Technology (Full).option4: ঘ) Destructive interference between waves of certain definite wavelengths.
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: In physics and optics, the Fraunhofer lines are a set of spectral absorption lines named after the German physicist Joseph von Fraunhofer. The lines were originally observed as dark features (absorption lines) in the optical spectrum of the Sun.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৫) The isotope of uranium capable of sustaining chain reaction is
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Uranium-235 has many uses such as fuel for nuclear power plants, and nuclear weapons such as nuclear bombs. Some artificial satellites, such as the SNAP-10A and the RORSATs were powered by nuclear reactors fueled with uranium-235.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৬) Which among the following is a positively charged particle emitted by a radioactive element?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Alpha particles, also called alpha rays or alpha radiation, consist of two protons and two neutrons bound together into a particle identical to a helium-4 nucleus.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৭) Nautical mile is a unit of distance used in:
General Science & Technology (Full).option2: খ) Measuring the boundaries of a nation
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: A nautical mile is a unit of measurement used in air, marine, and space navigation, and for the definition of territorial waters. Historically, it was defined as one minute (1/60 of a degree) of latitude along any line of longitude. Today the international nautical mile is defined as exactly 1852 metres (about 1.15 miles). The derived unit of speed is the knot, one nautical mile per hour.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৮) Electric current is measure by:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: An ammeter (from Ampere Meter) is a measuring instrument used to measure the current in a circuit. Electric currents are measured in amperes (A), hence the name. Instruments used to measure smaller currents, in the milliampere or microampere range, are designated as milliammeters or microammeters.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৯) One horse power is equal to
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Horsepower (hp) is a unit of measurement of power, or the rate at which work is done, usually in reference to the output of engines or motors.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১০) Decibel is the unit for
General Science & Technology (Full).exp:
A sound unit is any acoustic unit of sound measurement.
dB, decibel - noise of sound measurement is called decibels (dB). Ratio of the sound pressure to reference pressure to something.
Sone - a unit of perceived loudness equal to the loudness of a 1000-hertz tone at 40 dB above threshold, starting with 1 sone.
Phon - a unit of subjective loudness.
Hz, hertz - unit of sound frequency is called hertz (Hz)

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১১) Potassium Permanganate is used for purifying drinking water, because
General Science & Technology (Full).option1: ক) It is a reducing agent.
General Science & Technology (Full).option2: খ) It is an oxidising agent.
General Science & Technology (Full).option3: গ) It is a sterilising agent.
General Science & Technology (Full).option4: ঘ) It dissolves the impurities of water.
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Potassium permanganate oxidizes iron, manganese, and hydrogen sulfide into particles. The particles are then filtered with a multimedia filter which can be either manganese-coated aluminum silicate above manganese-treated green sand or an 8-inch layer of anthracite above manganese-treated greensand.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১২) Which of the following is the lightest metal?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp:
The lightest or least dense metal that is a pure element is lithium, which has a density of 0.534 g/cm3.
This makes lithium nearly half as dense as water, so if lithium was not so reactive, a chunk of the metal would float on water.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৩) Water is a good solvent of ionic salts because:
General Science & Technology (Full).option1: ক) It has a high specific heat
General Science & Technology (Full).option3: গ) It has a high dipole moment
General Science & Technology (Full).option4: ঘ) It has a high boiling point
General Science & Technology (Full).exp:
Water is a good solvent of ionic salts because it has a high dipole moment.
Salts are ionic compounds which, when dissolved in water, break up completely into ions.
They arise by the reaction of acids with bases, and they always contain either a metal cation or a cation derived from ammonium (NH4+).

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৪) Bell metal is an alloy of
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Bell metal is a hard alloy used for making bells and related instruments, such as cymbals. It is a form of bronze with a higher tin content, usually in approximately a 4:1 ratio of copper to tin (typically, 78% copper, 22% tin by mass).

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৫) LPG consists of mainly:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Liquefied Petroleum Gas or LPG consists mainly of methane, propane, propylene, butane, and butylene in various mixtures. It is produced as a by-product of natural gas processing and petroleum refining. The components of LPG are gases at normal temperatures and pressures.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৬) Permanent hardness of water can be removed by adding:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Sodium carbonate, Na2CO3, is also known as washing soda. It can remove temporary and permanent hardness from water. Sodium carbonate is soluble but calcium carbonate and magnesium carbonate are insoluble. The water is softened because it no longer contains dissolved calcium ions and magnesium ions.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৭) The filament of an electric bulb is made of
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The filament of an electric bulb is made of tungsten because it has some amazing properties including the highest melting point (3422<sup>o</sup>C), lowest vapor pressure, and greatest tensile strength out of all the metals. Because of these It can reach high temperature before melting.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৮) The two elements that are frequently used for making transistors are:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electronic signals and electrical power. Most transistors are made from very pure silicon, and some from germanium, but certain other semiconductor materials are sometimes used.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ১৯) What is laughing gas?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp:
Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or nitrous, is a chemical compound, an oxide of nitrogen with the formula N2O.
Nitrous oxide has significant medical uses, especially in surgery and dentistry, for its anaesthetic and pain reducing effects

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২০) Which of the following is in liquid form at room temperature?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The only liquid elements at standard temperature and pressure are bromine (Br) and mercury (Hg). Although, elements caesium (Cs), rubidium (Rb), Francium (Fr) and Gallium (Ga) become liquid at or just above room temperature.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২১) Soda water contains
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Carbonated water or Soda water is water that has been infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure. This produces a bubbly drink that's also known as sparkling water, club soda, soda water, seltzer water and fizzy water. With the exception of seltzer water, they usually have salt added to improve the taste.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২২) Carbon, diamond and graphite are together called:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Carbon is capable of forming many allotropes (structurally different forms of the same element) due to its valency. Well-known forms of carbon include diamond and graphite.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৩) The element common to all acids is
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: All acids contain hydrogen, but not all hydrogen-containing compounds are acids. Most acids also contain oxygen.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৪) Heavy water is:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Heavy water (deuterium oxide, 2H2O, D2O) is a form of water that contains only deuterium (2H or D, also known as heavy hydrogen) rather than the common hydrogen-1 isotope (1H or H, also called protium) that makes up most of the hydrogen in normal water.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৫) Galvanised iron sheets have a coating of
General Science & Technology (Full).exp:
Galvanisation is a process of coating ''Iron or Steel'' with Zinc to protect it from the Rusting.
Zinc ''weathers at a very slow rate'', so the coating protects the inner metal and provides it a very long life.
This process intact the steel with full strength and provide a more delightful appearance.
Zinc has a greater electronegativity than iron and provides a specific protection to the ''steel from the outer environment''.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৬) The hardest substance available on earth is
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Diamond is the hardest natural material known, where hardness is defined as resistance to scratching and is graded between 1 (softest) and 10 (hardest) using the Mohs scale of mineral hardness. Diamond has a hardness of 10 (hardest) on this scale.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৭) Washing soda is the common name for
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Washing soda is a chemical compound that can be used to remove stubborn stains from laundry. It is the common name of sodium carbonate. The sodium carbonate ''softens'' water helping other cleaning agents lift dirt particles from the fabrics and suspend them in the wash water.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৮) The gas usually filled in the electric bulb is
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Incandescent light bulbs are filled with an inert gas like nitrogen, argon, or krypton - so that the filament doesn't catch fire. Early ones were a vacuum. Flourecent lamps are filled with an inert gas plus mercury vapour or neon, which glows ultra-violet when charged. The inside of the bulb is painted to give it colour.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ২৯) Which of the following is used in pencils?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: A pencil is an implement for writing or drawing. It is a thin core of graphite well mixed with clay, inside a wooden body as protective casing that prevents the core from being broken.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩০) Which of the following is a non metal that remains liquid at room temperature?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Bromine is a chemical element with symbol Br and atomic number 35. It is the third-lightest halogen, and is a fuming red-brown liquid at room temperature that evaporates readily to form a similarly coloured gas. Its properties are thus intermediate between those of chlorine and iodine.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩১) The first graphical browser for the WWW was named:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: NCSA Mosaic, or simply Mosaic, was the web browser that popularized the World Wide Web and the Internet.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩২) What is the World Wide Web?
General Science & Technology (Full).option1: ক) The part of the Internet that enables information-sharing via interconnected pages
General Science & Technology (Full).option2: খ) Another name for the Internet
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The World Wide Web is a subset of the Internet. Specifically, the Web is a collection of documents and applications residing on Internet servers around the world.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৩) Which of the following word processors came first?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Before the invention of word processing and spreadsheet software, personal computers had little value in the mainstream business world. WordStar was used before the days of function keys and the mouse. It, instead, used a set of Ctrl and Alt key combinations to navigate and edit text documents.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৪) Which one of the following is a search engine?
General Science & Technology (Full).option2: খ) Librarians' Index to the Internet
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: A search engine is a program that searches for Web documents with keyword (s) you specify. Yahoo!, Google, Bing and AltaVista are just some examples of search engines that have been created to help you find information on the Web.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৫) What is a GPU?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: It is a chip dedicated to performing 3D calculations.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৬) HTML is used to
General Science & Technology (Full).option3: গ) Translate one language into another
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৭) In which decade was the transistor invented?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: On December 23, 1947, William Shockley, Walter Brattain and John Bardeen, of Bell Labs, announced their discovery of the point-contact germanium transistor to management.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৮) What are three types of lasers?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The first laser was a solid state laser. Solid state refers to any solid material like a glass rod. Diode lasers are very common because they are used to read compact disks and digital video disks in computers, CD players, and DVD players. Before diode lasers, the most common type of laser may have been the helium-neon laser, in which the active medium is a combination of the two gasses helium and neon.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৩৯) What was the first ARPANET message?
General Science & Technology (Full).option4: ঘ) Marry had a little lamb.
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Charley Kline Sends the First Message Over the ARPANET. The message was simply ''Lo'' instead of the intended word,''Login.''

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪০) What does AM mean?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Amplitude modulation was the first type to be used in radio. It works well with HF and morse code.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪১) What does VVVF stand for?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: It is a method of controlling the speed of an AC induction motor, whereby speed, current and torque can all be accurately controlled.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪২) Which is a type of Electrically-Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: It's commonly used for MP3 players, computer BIOS code and ''thumb'' drives. Originally developed in Japan by Toshiba, it has become quite popular for products requiring non-volatile erasable memory. Flash devices have a limited number of erase cycles (typically 10,000 to 1,000,000 cycles) so they're not as good a choice for applications in which the data changes constantly. However, since it has no moving parts (unlike a hard disk) it is an excellent choice for storing the operating code for small personal electronics like PDAs, cell phones, digital cameras, and the data in items like MP3 players.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৩) Glass is made of the mixture of:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The most familiar, and historically the oldest, types of manufactured glass are ''silicate glasses'' based on the chemical compound silica (silicon dioxide, or quartz), the primary constituent of sand.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৪) The type of glass used in making lenses and prisms is
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Flint glass is used in opticals and prisms. Flint glass is optical glass that has a relatively high refractive index and low Abbe number. A concave lens of flint glass is commonly combined with a convex lens of crown glass to produce an achromatic doublet lens because of their compensating optical properties, which reduces chromatic aberration.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৫) Which one of the following is the petroleum wax?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Paraffin wax is obtained from petroleum by dewaxing light lubricating oil stocks. It is used in candles, wax paper, polishes, cosmetics, and electrical insulators. It assists in extracting perfumes from flowers, forms a base for medical ointments, and supplies a waterproof coating for wood. In wood and paper matches, it helps to ignite the matchstick by supplying an easily vaporized hydrocarbon fuel.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৬) The abiotic and biotic components constitute the structure of an
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: Biotic components are the living things that shape an ecosystem. Examples of biotic components include animals, plants, fungi, and bacteria. Abiotic components are non-living components that influence an ecosystem. Examples of abiotic factors are temperature, air currents, and minerals.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৭) AIDS is caused by:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp:
Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) is a chronic, potentially life-threatening condition caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). By damaging your immune system, HIV interferes with your body's ability to fight infection and disease.
HIV is a sexually transmitted infection (STI). It can also be spread by contact with infected blood or from mother to child during pregnancy, childbirth or breast-feeding. Without medication, it may take years before HIV weakens your immune system to the point that you have AIDS.
There's no cure for HIV/AIDS, but medications can dramatically slow the progression of the disease. These drugs have reduced AIDS deaths in many developed nations.

.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৮) Which layer protects earth from harmful rays of the Sun?
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The ozone layer protects us from harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৪৯) The percentage of oxygen present in air is approximately-
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The air in Earth’s atmosphere is made up of approximately 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen. Air also has small amounts of lots of other gases, too, such as carbon dioxide, neon, and hydrogen.

General Science & Technology (Full).question: ৫০) Newton is the unit of:
General Science & Technology (Full).exp: The newton is the International System of Units (SI) derived unit of force. It is named after Isaac Newton in recognition of his work on classical mechanics, specifically Newton's second law of motion.
